```{r libraries, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta}
# Two rxode2 messages are expected here and muffled by name only: the
# occasion-indicator expansion makes the between-occasion etas
# non-mu-referenced (relevant to SAEM estimation, not to simulation), and the
# typical-value solves below run several subjects with the random effects
# removed.
muffle_known <- function(w) {
  msg <- conditionMessage(w)
  if (grepl("etas defaulted to non-mu referenced", msg, fixed = TRUE) ||
      grepl("multi-subject simulation without", msg, fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
mod <- readModelDb("Rabie_2020_abacavir")
mod_ui <- withCallingHandlers(rxode2::rxode(mod), warning = muffle_known)
mod_typ <- withCallingHandlers(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), warning = muffle_known)
```

* Citation: `r mod_ui$reference`
* Description: `r mod_ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.01923-19> (open access, PMC7179606)

Rabie 2020 describes abacavir pharmacokinetics in young South African
children with HIV and tuberculosis who needed lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) and
rifampin at the same time. To counter rifampin's induction of lopinavir
metabolism, extra ritonavir was added during TB treatment ("superboosting",
LPV/r 4:4). The model quantifies how this regimen changes abacavir exposure
relative to standard LPV/r 4:1 once rifampin has stopped.

# Population

Eighty-seven children (weight 3 to 15 kg at enrolment) were studied at five
South African sites between 2013 and 2015 (NCT02348177). Each child had
intensive sampling (predose and 1, 2, 4, 6 and 10 h after an observed morning
dose) at up to three visits: PK visit 1 in the second month and PK visit 2 in
the last month of TB treatment, both on rifampin + LPV/r 4:4, and PK visit 3
four to six weeks after standard LPV/r 4:1 had been reinstated (Rabie 2020
Table 1):

| | PK visit 1 | PK visit 2 | PK visit 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Children (male, %) | 86 (43) | 74 (36) | 71 (39) |
| Median (IQR) age, months | 19 (4 to 64) | 23 (8 to 68) | 26 (10 to 70) |
| Median (IQR) weight, kg | 8.7 (3.9 to 14.9) | 9.6 (5.7 to 15.9) | 10.2 (6.8 to 15.9) |
| Median weight-for-age Z-score | -2.43 | -1.93 | -1.50 |
| Median abacavir dose, mg/kg BID | 9.52 | 9.72 | 9.60 |
| Rifampin + LPV/r 4:4 | yes | yes | no |

Abacavir was given as a 20 mg/mL oral solution by the weight bands of Rabie
2020 Table 4. The metadata are available programmatically as
`mod_ui$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries a trailing source comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Rabie_2020_abacavir.R`; the table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location (Rabie 2020) |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` | log(9.67) L/h | Table 2, clearance (9.4 kg child on LPV/r 4:1) |
| `lvc` | log(8.76) L | Table 2, central volume |
| `lvp` | log(3.32) L | Table 2, peripheral volume |
| `lq` | log(1.35) L/h | Table 2, intercompartmental clearance |
| `lka` | log(2.22) 1/h | Table 2, absorption rate constant |
| `lmtt` | log(3.60 / 60) h | Table 2, absorption mean transit time 3.60 min |
| `lnn` | log(1.03) | Table 2, number of transit compartments |
| `lfdepot` | fixed(log(1)) | Table 2, bioavailability "1 (fixed)" |
| `ltlag` | log(2.62) h | Table 2, delay in absorption for night dose |
| `e_wt_cl_q`, `e_wt_vc_vp` | fixed 0.75, fixed 1 | Methods, allometric exponents; Table 2 footnote c (9.4 kg reference) |
| `ltm50_cl` | log(10.7) months | Table 2, PMAGE50 |
| `lhill_cl` | log(4.35) | Table 2, gamma |
| `e_rif_lpvr4_fdepot` | -0.360 | Table 2, LPV/r-4:4 + rifampin effect on bioavailability -36.0% |
| `etalcl`, `etalvp`, `etalq` | log(1 + CV^2) of 14.4, 29.0, 13.5% | Table 2, BSV; footnote a (lognormal, reported as CV) |
| `etabvv_cl_1..3` | log(1 + 0.184^2) | Table 2, CL BVV 18.4% |
| `etabvv_tlag_1..3` | log(1 + 0.099^2) | Table 2, night-dose delay BVV 9.90% |
| `etaiov_ka_1..6` | log(1 + 0.555^2) | Table 2, ka BOV 55.5% |
| `etaiov_fdepot_1..6` | log(1 + 0.448^2) | Table 2, bioavailability BOV 44.8% |
| `etaiov_mtt_1..6` | log(1 + 1.75^2) | Table 2, MTT BOV 175% |
| `propSd` | 0.230 | Table 2, proportional error 23.0% |
| `addSd` | 0.000310 mg/L | Table 2, additive error 0.310 ug/L |
| additive floor `0.2 * 0.0243` mg/L | 0.00486 mg/L | Methods: additive error bound to at least 20% of the LLOQ (0.0243 ug/mL) |
| Maturation `PAGE^hill / (tm50^hill + PAGE^hill)` | -- | Equation 1 |
| Two-compartment disposition, transit absorption | -- | Results, first paragraph |
| Occasion structure (each dose an occasion; evening + morning dose = one visit) | -- | Methods, Statistical analysis (i) |

# Typical-value checks

## Maturation of clearance (Figure 2)

Equation 1 is used as printed, so `lcl` is the clearance of a fully mature
9.4 kg child. The Results state that maturation reaches half its mature value
at about 2 months and is essentially complete by about 2 years of age
(postmenstrual age = postnatal age + 9 months).

```{r maturation}
mat <- function(page) page^4.35 / (10.7^4.35 + page^4.35)
mat_df <- tibble(pna_months = seq(0, 48, by = 0.25)) |>
  mutate(fmat = mat(pna_months + 9))

stopifnot(
  abs(mat(10.7) - 0.5) < 1e-12,
  mat(24 + 9) > 0.99,
  abs(mat(2 + 9) - 0.5) < 0.05
)

ggplot(mat_df, aes(pna_months, fmat)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(12, 24), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Postnatal age (months; PMA = PNA + 9)",
    y = "Fraction of mature clearance",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Rabie 2020."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Steady-state exposure against its closed form

With random effects removed, steady-state AUC over a dosing interval must equal
`F * dose / CL`. For a fully mature 9.4 kg child receiving 80 mg twice daily
(the 9-9.9 kg band of Table 4), that is 80 / 9.67 = 8.27 mg*h/L on LPV/r 4:1
and 0.64 times that on rifampin + LPV/r 4:4. Both sides use the same
parameters, so the bound is tight.

```{r closed-form}
cf_events <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = 1L, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = 0L),
  tibble(id = 2L, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = 1L)
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(
    bind_rows(
      tibble(time = seq(0, 72, by = 12), evid = 1L, amt = 80),
      tibble(time = seq(72, 84, by = 0.02), evid = 0L, amt = 0)
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    cmt = "depot", WT = 9.4, PAGE = 600, OCC = 0L, DOSETIME_EVENING = 0L
  ) |>
  mutate(cmt = ifelse(evid == 0L, "central", cmt)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

cf_sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = cf_events, returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = muffle_known
)

cf_conc <- cf_sim |>
  filter(time >= 72, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time = time - 72, treatment = ifelse(id == 1, "LPV/r 4:1", "RIF + LPV/r 4:4")) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
cf_dose <- tibble(
  id = 1:2, treatment = c("LPV/r 4:1", "RIF + LPV/r 4:4"), time = 0, amt = 80
)
cf_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(cf_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(cf_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, auclast = TRUE)
))
cf_auc <- as.data.frame(cf_nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(expected = 80 * c(1, 1 - 0.36)[match(treatment, c("LPV/r 4:1", "RIF + LPV/r 4:4"))] / 9.67)

knitr::kable(
  cf_auc |>
    select(treatment, PPORRES, expected) |>
    rename("Regimen" = treatment, "PKNCA AUC0-12" = PPORRES, "F * dose / CL" = expected),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical steady-state AUC0-12 (mg*h/L), 9.4 kg mature child, 80 mg BID."
)
stopifnot(all(abs(cf_auc$PPORRES / cf_auc$expected - 1) < 0.005))
```

## Higher morning predose than 10-h concentrations (Table 3)

The authors observed that the morning predose concentration (C0) was higher
than the 10-h concentration (C10) and explained it with an extra absorption
delay on the evening dose taken at home the night before. With the delay
switched on (`DOSETIME_EVENING = 1` on that dose) the typical C0 must exceed
C10; switching it off removes the effect.

```{r night-delay}
nd_events <- function(evening_flag) {
  doses <- tibble(time = seq(0, 72, by = 12), evid = 1L, amt = 80, cmt = "depot") |>
    mutate(DOSETIME_EVENING = as.integer(time == 60) * evening_flag)
  obs <- tibble(time = c(71.99, 82), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", DOSETIME_EVENING = 0L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(id = 1L, WT = 9.4, PAGE = 600, OCC = 0L, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = 0L) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
c_with <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = nd_events(1L), returnType = "data.frame")
c_without <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = nd_events(0L), returnType = "data.frame")
nd_tab <- tibble(
  `Evening-dose delay` = c("on (2.62 h)", "off"),
  `C0 (mg/L)` = c(c_with$Cc[1], c_without$Cc[1]),
  `C10 (mg/L)` = c(c_with$Cc[2], c_without$Cc[2])
)
knitr::kable(nd_tab, digits = 4, caption = "Typical C0 and C10 around the observed morning dose (9.4 kg, LPV/r 4:1).")
stopifnot(c_with$Cc[1] > c_with$Cc[2], c_without$Cc[1] < c_without$Cc[2])
```

# Virtual cohort

Separate cohorts of 200 children are drawn for each PK visit. Ages are
lognormal around the visit medians of Table 1; weights are approximate WHO
median weight-for-age values scaled down in proportion to the visit's median
weight-for-age Z-score (7.5% of the median per Z unit, chosen so that the
cohort's median weights approximate Table 1), restricted to the 3 to 15.9 kg
range of the study. Doses follow the weight bands of Rabie 2020 Table 4.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2020)
set.seed(2020)
n_per_visit <- 200

who_age <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72)
who_wt <- c(3.3, 4.4, 5.4, 6.1, 6.6, 7.6, 8.6, 9.4, 10.8, 12.0, 14.1, 16.1, 18.1, 20.2)
wt_per_z <- 0.075
who_median_wt <- function(age_months) approx(who_age, who_wt, xout = pmin(age_months, 72), rule = 2)$y

abacavir_dose <- function(wt) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    wt < 5 ~ 40, wt < 7 ~ 60, wt < 10 ~ 80, wt < 14 ~ 120, TRUE ~ 160
  )
}

visits <- tibble(
  visit = c("PK visit 1", "PK visit 2", "PK visit 3"),
  age_med = c(19, 23, 26),
  waz = c(-2.43, -1.93, -1.50),
  CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = c(1L, 1L, 0L),
  k = 1:3
)

draw_visit <- function(v) {
  out <- tibble()
  while (nrow(out) < n_per_visit) {
    cand <- tibble(
      AGE = pmax(3, v$age_med * exp(rnorm(400, 0, 0.84))),
      WT = who_median_wt(AGE) * (1 + wt_per_z * v$waz) * exp(rnorm(400, 0, 0.10))
    ) |>
      filter(WT >= 3, WT < 16, AGE <= 80)
    out <- bind_rows(out, cand)
  }
  out[seq_len(n_per_visit), ] |>
    mutate(visit = v$visit, k = v$k, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = v$CONMED_RIF_LPVR4)
}

cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(split(visits, visits$k), draw_visit)) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    PAGE = AGE + 9,
    amt = abacavir_dose(WT),
    band = cut(WT, c(3, 5, 10, 14, 17), right = FALSE,
               labels = c("3-4.9", "5-9.9", "10-13.9", "14-16.9"))
  )

cohort |>
  group_by(visit) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `Median age (months)` = median(AGE),
    `Median weight (kg)` = median(WT),
    `Median dose (mg/kg)` = median(amt / WT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual cohort by PK visit (compare Table 1).")
```

Each child takes abacavir every 12 h for three days. The evening dose at 60 h
is the home dose of the night before the visit (`DOSETIME_EVENING = 1`, occasion
`2k - 1`); the observed morning dose at 72 h starts occasion `2k`. Earlier doses
share the evening occasion, so the visit's clearance is constant over the run.

```{r events}
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(71.99, 72 + seq(0, 12, by = 0.25))))

cohort_cov <- cohort |>
  select(id, visit, band, k, WT, PAGE, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4)

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  select(id, k, amt) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 72, by = 12)) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
    DOSETIME_EVENING = as.integer(time == 60),
    OCC = ifelse(time < 72, 2L * k - 1L, 2L * k)
  )
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  select(id, k) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_grid) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, DOSETIME_EVENING = 0L,
    OCC = ifelse(time < 72, 2L * k - 1L, 2L * k)
  )
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  left_join(cohort_cov |> select(-k), by = "id") |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, WT, PAGE, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4, DOSETIME_EVENING, OCC) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = muffle_known
) |>
  left_join(cohort_cov |> select(id, visit, band), by = "id") |>
  mutate(tad = time - 72)
```

## Concentration-time profiles by visit (Figure 1)

```{r vpc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(tad >= 0) |>
  group_by(visit, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.0243, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~visit) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after observed morning dose (h)",
    y = "Abacavir (mg/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles with residual error.",
      "Dotted line: LLOQ 0.0243 mg/L. Replicates the layout of Figure 1 of Rabie 2020."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

AUC0-12 and Cmax are computed with PKNCA over the interval after the observed
morning dose, from the individual predictions (`Cc`, no residual error), per
visit.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(tad >= 0, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(id, treatment = visit, time = tad, Cc)
nca_dose <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, treatment = visit, time = 0, amt)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)
))
summary(nca_res) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated NCA after the observed morning dose, by PK visit.")
```

## Comparison with the published model-predicted exposures (Table 3)

```{r compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,   ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "PK visit 1", 6.36,     3.32,
  "PK visit 2", 7.01,     3.34,
  "PK visit 3", 10.2,     4.93
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("auclast", "cmax"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("PK visit" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = paste(
      "Median simulated AUC0-12 and Cmax versus the medians of Rabie 2020 Table 3.",
      "* differs from the published median by more than 20%."
    )
  )

auc_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(published, by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (med / auclast - 1))
# The published values are post hoc medians of the real cohort; the virtual
# cohort only approximates their weight and age mix, so each visit's centre is
# held to 20%; a wrong clearance, dose or bioavailability effect moves it more.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_med$pct) < 20))

# The regimen effect: visit 3 (LPV/r 4:1) over visits 1-2 (rifampin + 4:4).
ratio <- auc_med$med[auc_med$treatment == "PK visit 3"] /
  mean(auc_med$med[auc_med$treatment != "PK visit 3"])
cat(sprintf("Median AUC0-12 ratio, visit 3 / visits 1-2: %.2f (published 10.2 / 6.7 = %.2f)\n",
            ratio, 10.2 / mean(c(6.36, 7.01))))
```

## AUC0-12 by weight band and visit (Figure 4)

```{r figure4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
auc_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, band), by = "id")
ggplot(auc_ind, aes(band, PPORRES)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "salmon", outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6.02, colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 26)) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight band (kg)", y = "AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)",
    caption = "Red line: adult reference median AUC0-12 6.02 mg*h/L. Replicates Figure 4 of Rabie 2020."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Dosing simulation by weight (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows the steady-state AUC0-12 for Table 4 doses in 1-kg bands from
3 to 15 kg, on rifampin + LPV/r 4:4 and on LPV/r 4:1. The medians are
reproduced here with typical values (no random effects), at each band's
midpoint weight and an age from the same approximate weight-for-age relation
(Z = -2). The 3 and 4 kg bands depend strongly on that age assumption through
maturation and are shown but not asserted. Published medians were read from
Figure 3 by the maintainers and are approximate (about +/- 0.5 mg*h/L).

```{r figure3}
age_for_wt <- function(wt) {
  grid <- seq(0, 72, by = 0.05)
  approx(who_median_wt(grid) * (1 - wt_per_z * 2), grid, xout = wt, rule = 2, ties = mean)$y
}
fig3 <- tibble(band_kg = 3:15) |>
  mutate(WT = band_kg + 0.5, AGE = age_for_wt(WT), PAGE = AGE + 9, amt = abacavir_dose(WT)) |>
  tidyr::crossing(CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = 0:1) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

f3_events <- bind_rows(
  fig3 |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 72, by = 12)) |> mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  fig3 |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(72, 84, by = 0.1)) |> mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
) |>
  mutate(OCC = 0L, DOSETIME_EVENING = 0L) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, WT, PAGE, CONMED_RIF_LPVR4, OCC, DOSETIME_EVENING) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

f3_sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = f3_events, returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = muffle_known
)
f3_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(f3_sim |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> mutate(time = time - 72) |> select(id, time, Cc),
                   Cc ~ time | id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(fig3 |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt), amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, auclast = TRUE)
))

fig3_pub <- tibble(
  band_kg = rep(3:15, 2),
  CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 = rep(1:0, each = 13),
  auc_pub = c(14, 9.5, 9.5, 7, 7, 5.5, 5, 7.5, 7, 6.5, 6, 7.5, 7.5,
              25.5, 15.5, 15.5, 11.5, 11.5, 10, 8.5, 12, 11.5, 10.5, 10, 12.5, 12)
)
fig3_cmp <- as.data.frame(f3_nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  left_join(fig3, by = "id") |>
  left_join(fig3_pub, by = c("band_kg", "CONMED_RIF_LPVR4")) |>
  mutate(
    regimen = ifelse(CONMED_RIF_LPVR4 == 1, "RIF + LPV/r 4:4", "LPV/r 4:1"),
    pct = 100 * (PPORRES / auc_pub - 1)
  )

fig3_cmp |>
  select(regimen, band_kg, AGE, amt, PPORRES, auc_pub, pct) |>
  arrange(regimen, band_kg) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Weight band (kg)" = band_kg, "Assumed age (months)" = AGE,
    "Dose (mg)" = amt, "Typical AUC0-12" = PPORRES, "Figure 3 median (read)" = auc_pub,
    "% diff" = pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical steady-state AUC0-12 (mg*h/L) by 1-kg weight band versus Figure 3.")

# Bands of 5 kg and above, where maturation is essentially complete.
chk <- fig3_cmp |> filter(band_kg >= 5)
stopifnot(abs(median(chk$pct)) < 10, quantile(abs(chk$pct), 0.9) < 20)
```

```{r figure3-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(fig3_cmp, aes(band_kg)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = PPORRES), fill = "palegreen3", colour = "darkgreen") +
  geom_point(aes(y = auc_pub), colour = "navy") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6.02, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight band (kg)", y = "AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Bars: typical-value simulation; points: medians read from Figure 3.",
      "Red dashed line: adult reference 6.02 mg*h/L. Replicates Figure 3 of Rabie 2020 (children)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Additive error floor.** Table 2 reports an estimated additive error of
  0.310 ug/L, but the Methods state that the additive error "for all samples
  was bound to be at least 20% of the lower limit of quantification",
  0.2 x 0.0243 = 0.00486 mg/L. The model applies the bound as
  `max(addSd, 0.00486)`, so the effective additive SD is 0.00486 mg/L.
  Whether the authors added the bound to the estimate or took the larger of
  the two is not stated; the two readings differ by under 7% of the effective
  SD.
* **Coefficient of variation.** Table 2 footnote a states that the random
  effects are lognormal and "reported as the coefficient of variation", so
  every variance is `log(1 + CV^2)`. The confidence intervals are SIR
  percentiles, which cannot discriminate this from `CV^2`; the difference is
  material only for the 175% MTT BOV (variance 1.40 versus 3.06).
* **Occasions.** "Each dose was treated as a separate occasion, while
  consecutive evening and morning doses were grouped within the same visit."
  The model therefore has six occasions (`OCC` 1-6: evening and morning dose of
  each of three visits) for the BOV on ka, F and MTT, and shares the visit-level
  BVV etas on CL and the evening-dose delay across each pair. `OCC` outside 1-6
  turns BOV and BVV off. Simulations beyond the study design must choose an
  occasion coding; this vignette assigns all doses before the observed morning
  dose to the evening occasion.
* **Evening-dose delay.** The model applies the 2.62 h delay to the unobserved
  evening dose before a PK visit (`DOSETIME_EVENING = 1`), the only dose it was
  fitted to. The authors do not say whether it reflects late dosing, food or
  diurnal variation; the Figure 3 replication omits it, as the published
  steady-state dosing simulations describe children "dosed every 12 h".
* **Maturation reference.** Equation 1 is not normalised to a reference age,
  so the typical clearance of 9.67 L/h is the fully mature value; for the
  median-age child of the data set the maturation factor is about 0.98.
* **Postmenstrual age** is postnatal age + 9 months for every child, as in the
  source.
* **rxode2 mu-referencing message.** The occasion-indicator expansion routes
  the between-occasion and between-visit etas through intermediate variables,
  so rxode2 reports them as non-mu-referenced at parse. This matters for SAEM
  estimation only, not for simulation, and is the construction used by the
  other occasion-variability models in the library (e.g. Kengo 2025
  atazanavir); the vignette muffles that one message.
* **BLQ data** were handled with the M6 method during estimation; this affects
  fitting only, not simulation.
* **Virtual cohort.** Rabie 2020 reports only summary demographics. Ages and
  weights here come from approximate WHO median weight-for-age values scaled by
  the reported Z-scores; the age-weight relation the authors used for their
  dosing simulations (a weight-for-age model from children with tuberculosis)
  is not reproduced. Adult extrapolations (25-59.9 kg, 600 mg once daily) in
  Figure 3 are not reproduced.
* **Table 3 comparison.** The published AUC0-12 and Cmax are medians of
  individual post hoc predictions in the real cohort; the comparison above uses
  stochastic simulations in the virtual cohort.
* **Errata.** Europe PMC lists no erratum, correction or comment linked to
  this article (PMID 32071055; checked 2026-11-27).
